title: Prime Video September 2024: Titles Leaving Amazon Streaming Service
text:
Prime Video is losing several films and series at the end of September 2024. Here is what subscribers should watch before these titles leave Amazon's streaming service.
Prime Video is set to remove a collection of films and series from its subscription service at the end of September 2024, giving subscribers a limited window to watch them before they leave the platform. The departures arrive as the streaming service continues to add new originals and older favorites for the fall season.
Among the titles leaving Prime Video are past seasons of several shows and a number of films that have been available to subscribers. The exact lineup reflects the rotating licensing deals that shape what is available on Amazon's streaming service each month.
Prime Video Departures at Month's End
The list of titles leaving Prime Video includes both television series and movies. Among the television titles are past seasons that have been streaming on the service and are now scheduled to exit at the end of September.
The removals are part of the regular churn of licensing agreements between Amazon and content owners. Once a title leaves Prime Video, it may return later or appear on another platform, depending on where its rights move next.
Subscribers who have these titles on their watchlists have only until the end of the month to finish them on Prime Video. After that date, the titles will no longer be included with a Prime Video subscription.
What Else Is Happening in Streaming
The end-of-month departures coincide with a broader fall season across streaming services, with new originals and returning favorites arriving throughout September. Netflix is highlighting new seasons of shows including Monster and The Gentlemen, along with a title about the Unabomber case, as part of its own fall lineup.
The competition among streaming platforms remains intense, with each service rotating its library to keep subscribers engaged. Prime Video continues to promote a large catalog of films, including titles such as Munich, as part of its current offerings.
For subscribers, the practical effect is a steady cycle of arrivals and departures that requires attention to release calendars. Titles that are available one month may be gone the next, and vice versa.
Timing and Subscription Details
The titles are scheduled to leave Prime Video at the end of September 2024. The exact departure date can vary by title and region, so subscribers should check the Prime Video interface for the specific removal notice on each film or series.
Prime Video is included with an Amazon Prime membership, and subscribers can also access it through a standalone subscription. Removing a title from the service does not affect a subscriber's membership, but it does change what is available to stream at no additional cost.
Viewers who want to keep watching a departing title after it leaves Prime Video may need to rent or buy it through a digital storefront or find it on another streaming service, depending on where its rights are held.
Why Streaming Libraries Change
Streaming libraries change because platforms license content for limited periods rather than owning most of it outright. When a license expires, the title leaves unless the platform renews the agreement or negotiates a new one.
This system gives services flexibility to refresh their catalogs and manage costs, but it also means subscribers cannot assume that a favorite title will remain available indefinitely. The same dynamic affects films and television series across all major platforms.
For Prime Video users, the end of September is a reminder to check watchlists and prioritize anything scheduled to leave. The titles that are departing represent a mix of older series and films that have been part of the service's rotating catalog.
As the fall season progresses, more titles will arrive and others will depart, continuing the regular rhythm of the streaming business. Subscribers who follow these changes closely can make the most of their subscriptions without missing something they intended to watch.
